¹ A **review ceiling**, not a prescription: only restrict potassium if your blood potassium is high; your care team sets the number. 
² Used when blood phosphate runs high; phosphate additives count most (see the Phosphorus page). 
³ Total from food, supplements and calcium-based binders. 
⁴ Hemodialysis: 1,000 mL plus your measured urine output (1,500 mL assumes about 500 mL of urine). Peritoneal dialysis: set from your urine output and ultrafiltration.

Protein: with diabetes, never below 0.8 g/kg before dialysis (ADA 2026 Rec 11.3; KDIGO 2022 and 2024). Without diabetes, KDOQI 2020 allows 0.6–0.8 g/kg only under close clinical supervision. "Per kg" means per kg of a reference weight your team chooses; the 70 kg column is an example. Energy: KDOQI 2020 gives 25–35 kcal/kg; on peritoneal dialysis subtract the calories absorbed from the dialysis fluid (often 400 or more a day).
